links.outcome: Over-refusal of benign in-scope health prompts across 30 LLMs
links.effect: Safety-optimised models frequently refuse up to 80% of "Hard" benign prompts; larger frontier models show higher over-refusal than smaller or MoE-based models.
links.quote: We evaluate 30 state-of-the-art LLMs, including GPT-5 and Claude-4, revealing a significant tension: safety-optimised models frequently refuse up to 80% of "Hard" benign prompts, while domain-specific models often sacrifice safety for utility.

unlisted_practices: Benchmarking safe completion (high-level safe guidance on dual-use or borderline health queries) as an alternative to binary refusal

screen.reason: Empirical study introducing and evaluating LLMs on Health-ORSC-Bench, a benchmark designed to assess safety alignment, over-refusal, and safe completion quality in healthcare contexts without testing a specific organizational deployment practice.
